topic: Fixed-radius circle vertices and two-neighbor growth from arbitrary collinear triangular-lattice seeds
title: Shannon's circle-vertex conjecture and the Markey–Pfoertner seed-growth relation: an expanding-hexagon proof

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We prove Shannon's three conjectured circle-vertex formulas in OEIS A374338, FORMULA (revision 4, 5 July 2024; retained in revision 21), by identifying circle intersections with two-neighbor growth on the triangular lattice. The vertex count after n >= 1 steps is (3*n^2 + 5*n + c_r)/3, where r = n mod 3 and (c_0,c_1,c_2) = (0,4,2). A strip-clipped hexagon describes every collinear seed length, and becomes an unclipped hexagon at the sharp threshold n >= max(2,m-3) for m seeds and n >= 2. Its counts prove the three- and four-seed formulas recorded by Markey and the conjectured five-seed difference relation observed by Pfoertner and recorded by Markey. Corollaries give the periodic second differences and the precise series identities linking Barker's circle-addition and petal generating functions.
summary: An all-iteration geometric proof of the circle-vertex formulas and all-collinear-seed strip-clipped shape, including the sharp eventual-hexagon threshold, width-three count differences, Markey's periodic second differences, and qualified Barker-series identities.

verification.written: Euclidean-to-lattice equivalence; strip-clipped shape for every m >= 2 and n >= 2; the sharp unclipped-hexagon threshold n >= max(2,m-3); eventual counts and width-three differences; all initial cases for m = 2,3,4,5; periodic second differences; generating functions and the shifted A264788 identity; petal-series algebra, distinct from geometric petal enumeration.

formal_sources.coverage: All three Euclidean circle-count formulas for arbitrary distinct starting points; finite-shape count difference.
Exact shape for m = 2 or 5 and n >= 2; unit-circle intersections at lattice centers remain on the lattice.
Five-seed lattice count equals the circle count plus 4*n + 7 for n > 1.
